items.claim: The onset warrant is misstated on the bytes. At MT 4:16 (WEB 4:19) Daniel is not the first speaker: the verse opens with third-person narration of Daniel's dismay, then the king speaks, and only then Daniel replies. What changes at this edge is the frame: the king's first person at MT 4:15 gives way to third-person reference to the king at MT 4:16, and that third-person frame then runs to MT 4:30. The row names the weaker and inexact ground (a change of speaker from the king to Daniel) and does not state the shift of person.
items.both_sides: Behind the edge: MT 4:15 is the king's own first-person charge, אֲנָ֖ה מַלְכָּ֣א נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֑ר (oshb:Dan.4.15). At the edge: MT 4:16 has עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֗ר (oshb:Dan.4.16), the king named in the third person and still speaking, before עָנֵ֤ה בֵלְטְשַׁאצַּר֙ וְאָמַ֔ר (oshb:Dan.4.16). So the far side supports the cut, and supports it by a shift of person that the row leaves unsaid; the cut itself stands. No PE or SAMEKH stands after MT 4:15 (MEASURED, WLC only), as the row says.

suggested_fix.fact: The onset rests on the shift from the king's first-person speech to third-person narration in which the king is named and speaks before Daniel answers; Daniel's reply is the third movement of the verse, not its opening.

The WEB quotation at WEB 4:22 = MT 4:19 binds to the pronoun that is the verse's one ketiv/qere word; the row discloses the site, so the duty is met.

Second finding, low, named 'duration phrase under a formula key': observed_substrate_signals lists the at-that-moment key for this row. The inventory holds MT 4:16 under that key, but the words there are כְּשָׁעָ֣ה חֲדָ֔ה (oshb:Dan.4.16), a phrase of duration (WEB 'for a while'), not the temporal formula that stands at MT 4:30. The row does not argue from it; the signal should not be read as a formula occurrence.
Third finding, low, named 'untiered count': strongest_rejected_alternative states 9 verses with no tier; the count is true (WEB 4:19-4:27).

items.claim: Two disclosure gaps, neither touching the cut. First, the English gloss in the tag at WEB 4:24 = MT 4:21 is six consecutive WEB words of that verse and stands without quotation form. Second, the WLC editorial notes at MT 4:22 (WEB 4:25), which record an anomalous form and a ketiv/qere that differs from BHS, are not disclosed although the row's span covers the verse. The Aramaic splice, the ketiv/qere list, the paseq and the zero-mark claim are all true.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 4:20 ends the recital of the watcher's words and MT 4:21 opens with the interpretation formula; no mark follows MT 4:20, as the row says. Close side: MT 4:24 ends Daniel's speech and opens with the connective the row calls 'therefore' (first word of oshb:Dan.4.24); MT 4:25 is the narrator's notice. No mark stands between MT 4:24 and MT 4:25, so the close is unmarked; the PE comes one verse later (see W2-013).

items.claim: The Masoretic layer bounds this one-verse row on one side only, and the row weighs only the rival that the mark already excludes. In the WLC mark layer no PE or SAMEKH stands anywhere between the PE after MT 3:30 and the PE after MT 4:25: the notice at MT 4:25 (WEB 4:28) is the last verse of the open section that begins at MT 3:31 (WEB 4:1), and nothing separates it from MT 4:24 (WEB 4:27). The mark therefore favours reading the notice as the close of what precedes. The row's rejected alternative is the forward merge; the backward merge into the interpretation unit is not named.
items.both_sides: Onset side (MT 4:24 / MT 4:25): no mark; the ground is a change from Daniel's speech to a narrator's sentence, כֹּ֣לָּא מְּטָ֔א עַל נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֖ר מַלְכָּֽא (oshb:Dan.4.25). The third-person frame is not new here, since it began at MT 4:16, so the onset rests on the end of the speech alone. Close side (MT 4:25 / MT 4:26): a PE, single-witness, then a time phrase and a new scene. The close is the stronger edge and the onset the weaker one; a one-verse row is defensible as a record of that tension, but its weaker edge is the one left unweighed.

suggested_fix.fact: The rival to weigh beside the forward merge is the backward one: the notice read as the close of the interpretation, since no paragraph mark divides it from the end of Daniel's speech and the open section that the petuchah closes runs up to and includes the notice.
